Goal
* Please remove the monospace formatting applied to "0", "[[n]]-1" and "1", as it causes the sentence to break into multiple lines and reduces readability.

* You may format "0" and "1" as {{constants}} instead.

* Please revise "leave the hallway, the token" to "cause the token to leave the hallway, it".

Game modes
* Consider disabling Reverse mode, as it may be too difficult to infer the task from the visible tests alone without a full statement. Besides, you've copied the full statement into the stub generator, which defeats the purpose of Reverse mode.

Constraints
* Please reduce the upper bound of [[n]] to 10, as [[n]] never exceeds 10 in the existing test cases.

* Please reduce the upper bound of [[t]] to 10, as a [[t]] value close to the upper bound is used in one existing test case only (and that case should also be adjusted accordingly). Alternatively, please add at least 4 pairs of cases that cover the full range of [[t]] more evenly.

Cases
* Test 4: Please reduce the value of [[t]] to 10 or below to align with Validator 4 (regardless of whether the constraint on [[t]] is changed).

* Please add 4 new pair of cases where [[n]] > 1 and [[t]] > [[n]] x 2, with the final state covering the following scenarios:

  • Test 5 and Validator 5: the token is moving towards smaller positions.

  • Test 6 and Validator 6: the token is moving towards larger positions.

  • Test 7 and Validator 7: the token ends at position 0.

  • Test 8 and Validator 8: the token ends at position [[n]]-1.

Thanks.
Thst seems like pretty basic mathmatics. Also work on your language, it's not larger, but higher positions.

I don't think the rewording is necessary: "larger positions" is an unambiguous way to refer to increasing position numbers, whereas "higher positions" could be interpreted as a spatial direction rather than a numerical ordering.
